Hi [~accountid:641d5e830e6828ab20269e6d] 

With regard to your previous response, overall, I completely agree with the proposed approach.

Just to clarify for [~accountid:5ad471a8bb811e2b3af9482a] , where Tatsiana says that _“We will need to implement this into the app along with the buttons “opt out” of those processings” -_ the consent toggle should be *off by default*, and Bolt will only be able to turn it on after the user was presented with the necessary information (can be a banner with a link to PP) and made an active action confirming its consent.

The user then should have an option to always turn off the toggle to withdraw their consent, as Tatsiana has said. This is in relation to both 1. consent for location based adv. 2. to receive offers from Bolt related to Bolt’s *partners* offers.

With regard to your comments [~accountid:5ad471a8bb811e2b3af9482a] 

# “_we can only use the delivery location for targeting purposes only if users have separately agreed to it. Including this information in Terms and Conditions and notifying users about this update wouldn’t work here?” -_ *correct,* [~accountid:641d5e830e6828ab20269e6d] *please also confirm.*
# _“Additionally, do I understand correctly that we cannot legally highlight any provider-specific offers, e.g. ‘'30% off from McDonald’s''?” -_ actually, IMO, we must indicate who is the sender of marketing communications.
# I know [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/2587067086/Third-Party+Offers|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/2587067086/Third-Party+Offers|smart-link]  says otherwise - but only re/ our “Partner Offers” feature, which is not fully GDPR compliant and seems to be a compromise between privacy and marketing. If you have a closer look, there is a note: _“We’re not allowed to mention any company name other than Bolt in our communications_ *_without prior consent from our users_*_;”._
# As in many cases it may be impossible to indicate the concrete third parties, I believe we could just inform users more generally, mentioning categories of partners when asking for third party marketing consent. Then, when a specific offer is sent, a specific partner can be mentioned.

Hi [~accountid:616d3535327da40069944aa1] 

Thank you for submitting your request to us.

I have summarised some information regarding our T&Cs on this topic for you, please see below.

*Is there such a clause in our passenger T&Cs?*

No. There is no such exact statement in the passenger T&Cs. 

*Is there such a clause in any of our other T&Cs?*

There is, however, a clause (5.2) in our Bolt Balance T&Cs  ([link|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/2IkcfVUEfvUTokfCLdwoRr/73be86ded6cfde272e2dff6ed887b603/Bolt_Balance_Terms_and_Conditions__effective_as_of_21.07.2022_.pdf]) which may come close to what you are looking for. Please see the clause referred to below, and the particular language relevant to this ticket marked in {color:#bf2600}red{color}.

{quote}_5.2. In case you do not have sufficient amounts available on your Bolt Balance to settle the entire_
_amount you owe as a result of your use of the Bolt app or your purchase or use of the goods_
_and services available on the Bolt app, then such amounts may be debited from both your Bolt_
_Balance (in the amount available)_ {color:#bf2600}_and any of your payment instruments added as payment_{color}
{color:#bf2600}_methods in your Bolt app (in the remaining amount)_{color}_._{quote}

*Do the Bolt Balance T&Cs apply in this case?*

The Bolt Balance T&Cs apply when Bolt Balance feature in the app is used - so it depends on whether or not the negative balance has been shown in this particular passenger’s account under Bolt Balance. Bolt Balance can namely have the function of displaying the amounts that the relevant passenger owes as a result of their use of the Bolt app, or their purchase or use of the goods and services available on the Bolt app . According to clause 1.1.1 of the Bolt Balance T&Cs, this includes the following situation:

{quote}_(a) [an example of when Bolt Balance can be used is when] we have been unable to charge you for any goods or services you purchased_
_using the Bolt app (because of a failed card payment, for example, including_
_in case amount payable for the goods or services You purchased was not_
_known at the time of making the purchase and the amounts available on Your_
_payment card turn out to be insufficient); or_ 

_(…)_{quote}

Please let me know if this answers your question or if there is anything else I can do to help. 

Best regards,

Ida

{noformat}#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail

HOST="${1:-test-cluster1.redis.internal}"

while true; do
  date
  USED=$(redis-cli -h $HOST info |grep used_memory:|cut -f 2 -d ':'|tr -d '\r\n')
  MAX=$(redis-cli -h $HOST info |grep maxmemory:|cut -f 2 -d ':'|tr -d '\r\n')
  echo "Host: $HOST, Used: $USED, Max: $MAX"

  if [[ $USED -lt $MAX ]]; then
    echo continue
    ruby load.rb | redis-cli --pipe -h $HOST 2> /dev/null
  else
    echo stop; exit 2;
  fi
done{noformat}

load.sh (custom %, 95 in example)

{noformat}#!/bin/bash
set -uo pipefail

HOST="${1:-test-cluster1.redis.internal}"

while true; do
  date
  USED=$(redis-cli -h $HOST info |grep used_memory:|cut -f 2 -d ':'|tr -d '\r\n')
  MAX=$(redis-cli -h $HOST info |grep maxmemory:|cut -f 2 -d ':'|tr -d '\r\n')
  echo "Host: $HOST, Used: $USED, Max: $MAX"

  if [[ $USED -lt $((MAX*95/100)) ]]; then
    echo continue
    ruby load.rb | redis-cli --pipe -h $HOST 2> /dev/null
  else
    echo stop; exit 2;
  fi
done{noformat}

The amended IP section is acceptable in light of your comment and purpose of this Agreement. Just one proposal to consider re license clause 7.5. The Agreement is governed by Estonian law, which allows them to terminate (without any reason) a perpetual license by giving 1 year prior notice. To avoid that risk, I would add in clause 7.5. that the license is valid as long as the Deliverable(s) are protected by copyright or any other intellectual property right.

Clause 7.5 also mentions that the license is irrevocable, but this issue (irrevocable vs perpetual license) has not been tested in local courts. If taking the risk of termination is acceptable for you, then no change is needed.

Best,

Indrek

Hi [~accountid:61dd8fc3f63ac80070cdf28a] 

Thank you for clarifying.

*What is ARN and what does it mean that we have received this report?*

To provide som background, the National Board for Consumer Disputes (ARN) is a public authority that functions roughly like a court, but _is_ +not+ a court. ARN’s main task is to impartially try disputes regarding claims against business operators filed by the consumer to ARN. Since ARN is not technically a court, ARN’s decisions are merely recommendations on how a certain dispute should be resolved. ARN's recommendations are not binding, but in the disputes where ARN’s recommendation is in favour of the consumer, the majority of companies follow them.

In light of this, the fact that we have received a prompt from ARN to reply to a user claim does not necessarily mean that ARN considers that we have done something wrong. It is only meant to give us an opportunity to protect our interests by giving our side of the story before ARN decides on its position in relation to the dispute. 

*Should we reply to ARN?*

Yes, I believe you should. Given that it seems pretty clear in this case that the user has parked in a manner that violates our T&Cs (see below), I think we should at least give it a go and reply to ARN with our position. All communications between the parties in a dispute handled by ARN are submitted in written form (no hearings, etc). 

*What should we reply to ARN?*

In summary, I recommend replying to ARN and explaining that the user has breached our Terms and Conditions for use of E-vehicles ([link|https://assets.ctfassets.net/tk7rwcciwvbq/lxZLg2GyvPx4Q04XdX8Gl/bc265559c9bb974194e41fdcdd073e9b/SE_Bolt_E-Vehicles_T_Cs__v_20230201_in_English_.docx.pdf]) (which the user has agreed to when downloading the app and starting to use our services), entitling us to claim the disputed amount from the user (see particularly sections 4.3 (4.3.3), 5.7 and 5.8). 

Please note that the exact formulation of the reply must be decided from a local ops perspective.

Please let me know if you have any additional questions, or if we can close the ticket.

Best regards,

Hi, [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2]! We have asked the external counsel about the issues related to consent and withdrawal. Here is the summary:

In case the rider uses their right to withdraw from the subscription during the withdrawal period Bolt will need to either decline refund or refund rider fully or partially. The course of action will depend on the scope of the benefits and text that we put in the T&Cs.

# No refund - we are able to benefit from the exclusion provided in Article 16 (a) of the [Consumer Rights Directive|https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A02011L0083-20220528&qid=1696249156977#E0003] (the “*Directive*”) that allows us to keep all money paid by the rider for the subscription if the following conditions are met:
## the benefits that we provide as part of the subscription are limited in quantity and are fully utilised before exercising the right of withdrawal;
## the rider has provided explicit consent to receive benefits during the withdrawal period;
## the rider is informed that they will lose their right for a refund once all benefits are utilised.
# Partial refund - in case we would not be able or willing to use exception provided in Article 16 (a) of the Directive we are able to issue a partial refund according to Article 14 (3) of the Directive if the following criteria is met:
## we inform the rider that they will be liable to pay Bolt reasonable costs in case they consent to the provision of the benefits during the withdrawal period (Article 6(1)(j) of the Directive);
## rider provides explicit consent to start receiving benefits during the withdrawal period (Article 8 (8) of the Directive). 
# Full refund - we will need to provide a full refund to the rider in case we do not benefit from points described above.

*Therefore, we need rider's explicit consent to receive benefits during the withdrawal period if we want to benefit from partial refund or decline refund. If we do not ask for their consent - we will need to refund all money paid by the rider.*

If we want to benefit both from partial refund and “no refund” options, then we need to add explicit consent, information that the rider will lose their right to claim a refund once all benefits are utilised and inform the rider that they will be liable to pay reasonable costs if they withdraw after having consented to the provision of the benefits during the withdrawal period.

The counsel thinks that Article 16 (a) exception may apply to us based on Lachlan’s message that some benefits will be limited in quantity, but you told me that benefits will be mostly unlimited ones that will be available throughout the duration of the subscription, in which case we can only rely on partial refund option. However, it is unclear whether we can rely on the exception in case benefits we provide are mix of two and user consumes the benefit that was limited in quantity entirely (I can clarify this with the counsel in case we are interested in declining the refund).

[~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2], can you please tell whether we want to exercise “no refund” and/or “partial refund” options so as we could decide on the final content of the T&Cs?

The point is of moving endpoints to RHB is specifically to use the same fee calculators for runtime (pre-order) calculations as we do for post-ride calculations (which results in record generation in RHB). Otherwise we’re running a risk of diverging between upfront calculations and post-ride, since at some point we may have to update fee calculators in RHB and not care about them in invoicing. Also, as highlighted in description, we don’t support (and don’t plan) indirect tax calculations in invoicing, so if {{getUpfrontFee}} is called from one of the countries which have them, we’ll return incorrect values there.

As a result, checkpoints became invalid and ingestion job fails on next run.

_Dear Europ Assistance team,_

_Thank you for your e-mail. We hope all is well with you._

_Based on article 28 EU VAT Directive, and respective national laws, a tax fiction is created that drivers provided transport services to Bolt, who then provided the same services to the Business customer. In this sense, from a tax law perspective, this situation is seen as a resale of transport services by Bolt. This tax law fiction of a resale is what makes it possible for Bolt to provide one single invoice (a summary invoice) to Europ Assistance. If Europ Assistance can demonstrate that the transport services were used by its users in its economic interests for its taxable activities, the taxable base is the amount of services included in the invoice and there should be no issue with claiming the input VAT._
_For clarity, the above setup can be considered resale only for the purposes of tax (VAT) laws to ensure reporting and payment of taxes. In the civil law nor in any other regulatory context Bolt is not reselling/providing transportation services. No T&C’s (Business nor Rides’) or factual circumstances (Bolt does not own nor manage the vehicles, manage drivers, nor does it hold any license/registration for the provision of the transportation services) support any narrative of such resale. Hence other than tax law, the single invoicing setup should be viewed as a mere billing technicality. Bolt pays and reports all taxes, as applicable, and recognises the revenue from the aggregated invoice as its own revenue._

_Best regards,_

Data loss refers to an incident where data is destroyed, deleted, or becomes inaccessible on a computer or data storage system.

It can occur through various means including human error, such as accidental deletion or overwriting, hardware failure like a hard disk crash, software bugs, or malicious activities like viruses and ransomware. Additionally, natural disasters can result in physical damage to storage devices, leading to data loss.

Generally, at Bolt, the types of data that could be lost may include:

# *User Data*: Personal information of users (riders and drivers, couriers, etc), including their trip histories, payment information, and contact details.
# *Operational Data*: Information on daily operations like trip logs, driver routes, and financial transactions.
# *Financial Data*: Billing records, driver earnings, and other financial data critical for both Uber and its stakeholders.
# *Analytical Data*

Hi [~accountid:616d3535327da40069944aa1], 

Thanks for raising this ticket. The topic of children travelling unattended with a driver via Bolt raises several questions and legal issues. 

*First*, *a minor is not capable of entering into any legally binding agreements pursuant to Chapter 9 section 1 of the* *_Swedish Family Act_**.* Consequently, a minor can’t accept our T&Cs or enter into a transportation service agreement with the driver. 

* If a minor indeed has managed (through using fake information or similar) to create an account with Bolt and accept the T&Cs, then such acceptance is invalid in itself and the account should be deleted. 
* If the ride was ordered by anyone other than the minor itself, then there is a valid contract with such person who ordered the trip, which means that no contract is in place with the actual passenger. Since the passenger is a minor and lacks the legal capacity to enter into any contracts, we can’t rely on the acceptance of the terms by somebody else on behalf of the minor. +_However, children are under the care of their parents and the parents hold the legal responsibility for their children which means that parents are free to put their child in a taxi if they deem it reasonable_+. 

*Second, since we have no age limit in the Passenger T&Cs which restricts anyone from ordering a ride for a minor, making such an order is currently not in breach with our T&Cs.* We are planning to do two things in Q4 on this topic:

* have a pop-up for all new riders entering our app where they need to confirm that they are at least 18 years old before starting to use our services
* add a wording to the Passenger T&Cs, according to which the riders need to be at least 18 years old in order to use our platform. 

By those implementations, we will prevent parents from ordering rides for their unattended children and any such order would be in breach of our T&Cs. 

*Third, we inform drivers that they may reject trips if they can identify that the riders are unattended minors although this is not directly stated in the Driver T&Cs.* Essentially we are giving the drivers the right to act - while not explicitly preventing such orders from being made. This leaves us in a tough position where parents may claim that they are allowed to make orders for their children while drivers reject such trips and the driver is allowed to do so since there is no valid transportation service agreement in place with the passenger and no explicit parental consent. This is what we aim to prevent with the updates mentioned above and unfortunately we currently aren’t in a position to do anything about these incidents. +_For the time being, drivers who reject minors are acting within their rights since (1) there is no valid contract and (2) there is no parental consent in regards to the transportation service and therefore the driver can refuse to complete the trip._+ 

*Last, there is no explicit limitation in Sweden on the appropriate age for children to be traveling alone in a taxi.* Usually the operators of transport services, such as train & flight operators, determine limitations in their own terms based on safety reasons. This is what we will do in the future with our 18+ age restriction in our T&Cs. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

Findings from Redis Cluster stress tests:

* Redis v6.2.11+ has an issue with failed sync on big clusters (>=7Gb). Uploaded 6.2.10 for both Ubuntu 20.04/22.04
* For 8 ,16 ,32Gb instances with 2 redises per node safest maxmemory are 3, 6, 12Gb. More or less stable maximums are 3.5, 7, 14Gb accordingly (keep in mind that in this case when cluster is full, high probability of getting memory used alerts > 95%). This will decrease total memory used on example of 7gb/r6g.large from 90% (maxmemory/total memory ratio) to 80% and 95% (total memory usage on host) to 78%
* inv redis-cluster.maintenance won’t work from start to end with big clusters, failing after each instance change (ticket to improve). But it safe to run it multiple times.
* I plan to enable oom-score-adj yes  option, which will optimize oom-killer in kernel to kill first background processes and then replicas and last master

After talking with Dmytro and Varvara we decided not to tackle this bug further.

On the BE side the effort would be big because we would need to ask the order team to expose a new endpoint on delivery-order to receive the latest order.

Currently, the pooling service has a cache that updates the data periodically from other services. When the order is completed, the cache is updated and a new event is triggered.

The user order history service listens to this event and updates the db.

Here is the race condition that we see. Sometimes the UI receives the changes from pooling, asks for the rating popup before the user history service manages to update the db. This results in rating popup returning null.

When the rating popup is called again, it will return the last order if the service had time to catch up with the latest changes.

Thank you for all of the comments.

*It seems to me that in this particular case there would not be much risk in proceeding with the posting without obtaining consent and additional privacy considerations.*

For the future, I am raising this issue with the privacy team as apparently we do not have any guidelines on how to conduct events from a privacy perspective - when and how to obtain consent for filming, etc.

As it's not an urgent matter, likely this will become a project we will work on in Q1 of 2024, and when it's ready - we will reach out.

*The basic recommendations would be*:

* before the event is conducted, where possible, publicly inform that it will be filmed and for what purposes - eg., posting in social media later, and also give people an opportunity to opt out. 
* This can be in the form of a simple instruction: “If you do not want to be filmed or appear in SM materials, please let the organisers know by email or approaching them on-site. If it's unclear who is the organiser, it should be clearly conveyed to the data subjects so they know whom to approach.
* On-site, a visible banner for this would work, like A3 paper. Single consent forms where everyone gives consent to be filmed usually are not necessary.
* Online announcements before the event would be ideal, on-site banner may not be the most practical solution, but both approaches can be used for the same event.
* instruct the photographer not to film children & minors, because in most situations we need an explicit consent from their parents for this.

The rules will differ in different EU countries, but these basic recommendations should allow us to be compliant in most jurisdictions, Ireland included.

Germany has the strictest laws from my experience, and additional guidelines may have to be checked for different countries.

h3. User travels to another country

Bolt Balance uses the currency of the country where the user is located.

If a user has a positive balance in one currency and travels to a country that uses a different currency, their Bolt Balance in that currency is saved and will be available as soon as the user returns.

Until the user returns to a country matching the currency of their balance, their Bolt Balance won't be visible in the app.

Due to regulations and not supporting currency conversion in the app, it is not possible to transfer a user's balance from one currency to another.

Hey [~accountid:5d95f00136d2520dde7ede17] 

* Yes, we have to provide tax reports to drivers even if they have deleted their account for as long as we retain this data.

Clarification: Individuals, in accordance with Article 15 of the GDPR, have the right to access the personal data collected about them. This right enables them to request a copy of their own data, including information related to tax reports.

Article 15(4) of the GDPR introduces limitations on this right, stipulating that access can be refused to the extent that it may negatively impact the rights and freedoms of other individuals. However, any refusal must be substantiated and cannot be based solely on a general reference to potential harm to others. This exception is unlikely to apply in the case of tax reports, as they typically do not contain personal data about other individuals.

In light of the GDPR's principles of data storage limitation (GDPR Article 5(1)(e)), the question is: how long do we retain driver’s tax reports in our systems? Since tax reports are related to accounting, the storage period should be set in the law (the accountant shall know how long such data is kept). Thus, we shall provide a copy of tax reposts to drivers upon their request as long as this data is kept within our system.

If there is a 30-day time delay between the incident and the reporting, investigating the circumstances becomes challenging. 

The general approach should be:

# Incident is reported to us;
# The scooter is taken offline and inspected, necessary tests are concluded (like brake checks, bearings etc).
# Findings are documented. If no fault is found, the process ends.
# If faults are found, we settle the matter with the user.

As a general remark: using the scooter in unsafe conditions (in dark, wet conditions, minus degrees) does not equal to a mechanical fault.

There are, yes, but they all are country specific, for example, in Estonia:

* The term for filing a claim for wages is three years as of the time the wages fell due.
* The time-limit for filing a claim for the recognition of rights arising from employment relationships and for the protection of violated rights for the purpose of recourse to a labour dispute committee or court is four months as of the time the person became or should have become aware of the violation of their rights.
* An employer’s claim for refund of wages and other financial claims arising from an employment relationship expire within 12 months as of the time when the employee received the wages or an advance payment of wages.
* An employer’s claim for compensation for damage against an employee for damage caused upon performance of duties expires within 12 months as of the time when the employer learnt or should have learnt of the damage caused and the person obligated to compensate for it, but not later than three years after the damage was caused.

In addition we also need to cover situations when Bolt have some legal dispute with the employee so the data needed for specific legal dispute is not deleted and we can present it to the relevant institutions or courts during all period of dispute.

There are two actions related to promo codes: *issuing* the code and *booking* the code. Everything is clear with booking - the code must be booked where it was used (if the code is used in the Centralized market, it should be booked by Bolt Operations). This part is clear as the promo code will always be used only in the country for which it was issued. In the promo code generator, you have to select a country, and the code can’t be used anywhere else (if it was created for Estonia, it will be valid only in Estonia).

However, I still have questions about *issuing* the code. So far, I understand that for Centralized markets, the promo code should be issued only by Bolt Operations. If the market is Local, the code should be issued only by that Local entity.

So far in our chat we have only {{seen ack}} and not {{delivery ack}}. When a {{Client A}} sends a message to a {{Client B}}, the server only knows that the message was sent to the {{Client B}}, but it doesn't mean that the message is delivered to the {{Client B}}. When the {{Client B}} opens the chat screen and the message becomes visible on it, the {{Client B}} sends the {{seen ack}}to the server, so it knows that the message was seen. 

In order to query the data you’d like to have in future we first need to implement the {{delivery ack}} in the clients and on the server.

{code:sql}SELECT x.key                                    AS key ,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id)                       AS count_of_users,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id)                      AS count_of_orders,
SUM(x.price_eur)                                AS sum_of_orders,
SUM(x.refund_eur)                               AS sum_of_refund_eur,
(SUM(x.refund_eur) * 1.0) / SUM(x.price_eur)    AS refund_sum_ratio
FROM (
    SELECT 
    o.delivery_address || ':' || co.country_code                AS key,
    co.user_id                                                  AS user_id,
    co.order_id                                                 AS order_id,
    co.user_price_eur                                           AS price_eur,
    co.user_price                                               AS price,
    COALESCE(co.refund_amount,0)/NULLIF(co.eur_currency_rate,0) AS refund_eur,
    COALESCE(co.refund_amount,0)                                AS refund
    FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co 
    LEFT JOIN ng_delivery_spark.delivery_order_order o ON co.order_id = o.id AND co.city_id = o.city_id AND o.created_date >= DATE(DATE_ADD(CURRENT_DATE, -90))
    WHERE co.created_date >= DATE(DATE_ADD(CURRENT_DATE, -90))
    AND co.order_type = 'food_delivery'
    AND co.order_state = 'finished'
    GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7
) AS x
GROUP BY 1
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT x.user_id) > 1 AND COUNT(DISTINCT x.order_id) > 1
AND SUM(x.refund_eur) > 10
AND (SUM(x.refund_eur) * 1.0) / SUM(x.price_eur) > 0.1{code}

Hi Team, as promised, reverting with the feedback concerning the advertisement of novelty tobacco products:

* In relation to selling, there is no material difference between heated products (Heets / Glo and Vapes), refillable e-cigarettes and normal cigarettes - all products (heated products, tobacco sticks (e.g. Heets), devices (e.g. IQOS), or refillable e-cigarettes, etc.) can be sold online, but only subject to age verification (checkbox "I'm over 18 year old") - so same as traditional cigarettes and tobacco products. The details [here|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gI-GsiCkIqV9vvyEPbRk0BhRXXfCSa8HqmTkPdRi5Lc/edit#gid=0]
* As regards advertising, formally heated products (Heets / Glo and Vapes) still escape the ban on advertisement addressed to the general public (such as on bilboards), as they are not assimilated to regular tobacco products because they are not technically used for "smoking", as per Law no. 457/2004 on tobacco advertising. 
* There is a draft law in Parliament aimed at correcting this loophole but it is not yet enacted. cc: [~accountid:60f2a71843c956007065f2ad] 
* Nonetheless, advertising them in-app without any age verification is borederline to offering them for sale (including to minors), therefore it is not risk free. It is, thus, safer, to advertise only in the smoking section of the app. Thus, formally - all these products escape the ban on advertisement - as they are not technically used for "smoking", including in the case of the display and advertising in the app; nevertheless, the age verification checkbox is recommended.
* Ancillary products such as rolling papers are not subject to restrictions (no restrictions/age verification requirements both for selling and advertising), but refilling devices (if they contain tobacco/nicotine) are subject to the same restrictions as tobacco products (age verification).

[~accountid:5de0e6d7b95b180d17cf1905] thank you for the input. The changes by the Web team would be a great start but - keeping in mind current recommendations/ guidelines by different data protection authorities, this would be considered to be a short term fix. Let me please explain this in more details. 

There is not legal requirement of a “privacy”-Button but by law we have to provide concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible information on privacy (intuitive, easy, fast). We are happy to work together to find solutions for this.

*How to get to the privacy notice easily/quickly:*

Splitting up the legal and the privacy- landing page on [http://bolt.eu|http://bolt.eu|smart-link]  is great progress but it made it harder for users to find the required information on data protection. If users currently want to find out about the privacy notice quickly and easily via the app, this requires the following steps:

# Open the Main Menu
# Enter the "About" Section
# Click the "Legal" button
# On the opened browser page, scroll to the bottom
# click on "Privacy" in the footer. 

* *Legal requirement:* 

The GDPR but also most other data protection laws require that companies which process personal data shall take appropriate measures to provide any specific information relating to processing of personal data to the data subject in a concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible form (Art 12, 13, 14 GDPR). 

The current access to the privacy notice involves several steps and is not very intuitive. Looking at the current decision practice of the European supervisory authorities and the available recommendations/ guidelines (published by the authorities), it seems questionable whether the requirement for an understandable and easily accessible form is met. 

Infringements of the provisions on providing information to the data subjects are subjects to administrative fines up to 20 000 000 EUR/ up to 4 % of the total worldwide annual turnover. 

* *Regulatory requirement*

The supervisory authority responsible for Bolt in most cases is the Estonian Data Protection Authority (AKI). Similar to the authorities in Ireland, this authority is under constant criticism or increasing pressure from other European authorities to act more often. Therefore, the former underfunded Estonian Data Protection Authority (AKI) has expanded its team by 60% in 2023 to increase enforcement. This is already leading to increased pressure (noticeable increase in procedures and requests). A focus of the authority is the transparency of data processing, and the authorities have already indicated that Bolt needs to work on this. 

Implementing a privacy button would not only raise compliance and minimise the potential risk of complaints but also show goodwill towards the main supervisory authority. FYI Bigger companies like TikTok and Meta were already fined in multiple European states (eg. [WhatsApp Ireland Ltd., € 225,000,000|https://dataprotection.ie/en/news-media/data-protection-commission-announces-conclusion-two-inquiries-meta-ireland]; [TikTok, € 14,500,000; |https://ico.org.uk/about-the-ico/media-centre/news-and-blogs/2023/04/ico-fines-tiktok-127-million-for-misusing-children-s-data/] D[eliveroo Italy s.r.l., € 2,500,000 (Partly because of failing to inform customers|https://www.gpdp.it/web/guest/home/docweb/-/docweb-display/docweb/9685994])[ |https://ico.org.uk/about-the-ico/media-centre/news-and-blogs/2023/04/ico-fines-tiktok-127-million-for-misusing-children-s-data/]

* *Common practice*

A cross-comparison with other apps (including direct competitors) has shown that many offer a privacy button. For an illustration, please refer to our American friend:

# open "account
# enter the "legal" section
# open the link "privacy policy

But preliminary:

understanding that we want to avoid communicating the offer directly to the couriers, and pretending that this is the offer from a third party (and not from Bolt), a specific consent from couriers to receive marketing comms from third parties *will be required by law*.

So, if the couriers do not opt in, we would not be able to share their details with Wear You Brand to send them the promotion of the bags.

This is different from what Adriana advised previously, but to be clear - for any third party marketing comms, an opt in consent will have to be obtained, no derogations.

Unfortunately, afaik, Bolt has not yet implemented a feature to receive third party consent apart from a toggle in settings for *riders* - so, basically, we do not have third party marketing consents for anyone else, including couriers.

This means that you can either:

1. take the risk and send out such comms without consent;

2. receive consent on case-by-case basis.

Practically, in this case this can be implemented as a notification banner with a tick box / toggle (UNTICKED/OFF by default). This is the legal way to do it.

I am not sure I would be able to share about the risks of not following the law - but we are currently experiencing attention from the Portuguese regulator for the violations of marketing activities and potentially fines, so I would advise to be careful.

h4. *Q: Why does the fleet/driver still see -0.01 or -0.02 balance, after paying the exact amount?*

This is a world wide accounting concept called “rounding”. It is a glitch that is not unique to Bolt. To explain it briefly, we show the balance entries with 2 decimals in admin (i.e. 31.78), however in the system it has more decimals (i.e. 31,784). And in Driver Portal, it is shown with 1 decimal only (i.e. 31.8). So when decimals get less, the system rounds it up/down to the closest number.

So, the system rounds the actual number up/down according to the decimals, which might result in cent differences. Our accounting system is smart enough to consider this number for the next payout.

[^DPA_Bolt_Operations_Leapsome_GmbH_10.10.2023.pdf]

Hi [~accountid:712020:adc75bb7-f145-4fbb-b5a0-0536b95ff918] 

In general use of use of psychometric tools for recruiting is not prohibited in EEA but it must be in compliance with data protection and employment laws.

From employment law side main principle to follow is equal treatment and non-discrimination, meaning that use of such tools as well as assessments of results should be done in a fair and non-discriminatory way that does not discriminate against certain applicants based on protected characteristics, such as race, gender, religion, or disability etc. Employment decisions should not be made solely based on the results of such assessments but they could be used alongside other recruitment methods and strategies. Employer should be able to provide information and proofs about how results of such assessment have been administrated and how they impacted hiring decision. 

From data protection side such assessments could be considered as processing of special category of personal data - data concerning health meaning that they must be processed according to Article 9 of GDPR. I would advise to ask opinion regarding this also from Data Protection team to understand better the actions needed to be taken by Bolt for using such tools in recruiting. From my understanding employer should receive explicit and informed consent from the candidate before use of such tool in recruiting.

Created an example query to get this data for an order, this can be used as starting point:
NB: the {{order_courier_id}} from {{delivery_order_order_courier_state_log}} is not the {{courier_id}} of the order, but the {{id}} of the {{delivery_order_order_courier}} table.

{noformat}select doo.created,
       doo.delivery_address,
       doo.delivery_lat,
       doo.delivery_lng,
       doo.provider_id,
       dop.lat as provider_lat,
       dop.lng as provider_lng,
       doc.courier_id,
       doc.type_of_vehicle,
       doc.state,
       doc.created,
       docs.created as state_created,
       docs.event_sent_timestamp,
       docs.event_state,
       docs.from_state,
       docs.to_state,
       docs.lat as state_lat,
       docs.lng as state_lng,
       docs.lat_lng_timestamp
from glue.ng_delivery.delivery_order_order doo
         LEFT JOIN glue.ng_delivery.delivery_order_order_provider dop ON (dop.order_id = doo.id AND dop.city_id = doo.city_id)
         LEFT JOIN glue.ng_delivery.delivery_order_order_courier doc ON (doc.order_provider_id = dop.id AND doc.city_id = dop.city_id)
         JOIN glue.ng_delivery.delivery_order_order_courier_state_log docs ON (docs.order_id = doo.id and docs.city_id = doo.city_id)
where
    doo.created_date between date '2023-10-01' and date '2023-10-05'
    and dop.created_date between date '2023-10-01' and date '2023-10-05'
    and doc.created_date between date '2023-10-01' and date '2023-10-05'
    and docs.created_date between date '2023-10-01' and date '2023-10-05'
    and doo.id = 138587826;{noformat}

h3. CONSIDERATIONS

The behavior currently reported above by best-offer:

* should be very *rare* 
* it is kind of a bug: the model should not return a category as “best offer” if there is one with better ETA and price

For these reasons we will “ignore” this corner case for now.


h3. VALIDATION

To add some validation on the above, I ran the below query in Presto, checking how many times the {{best_offer_category_id}} did *not* have the minimum pickup duration:

Results:

||*MONTH*||*total*||best_offer_not_fastest||best_offer_fastest||
|SEPTEMBER|213,063,195|0|213,063,195|

QUERY

{code:sql}WITH MinDurations AS (
    SELECT search_categories_overview_token, MIN(duration_till_pickup) AS min_duration
    FROM glue.core.search_categories_overview_category
    WHERE created_hour >= TIMESTAMP '2023-09-01 00:00:00.000' and created_hour < TIMESTAMP '2023-10-01 00:00:00.000'
    GROUP BY search_categories_overview_token
),
MinCheck as (
	SELECT sco.best_offer_category_id,
		scoc.search_categories_overview_token,
	    scoc.search_category_id,
	    scoc.pos,
	    scoc.duration_till_pickup,
	    CASE
	        WHEN scoc.duration_till_pickup = md.min_duration THEN TRUE
	        ELSE FALSE
	    END AS is_ok
	FROM glue.core.search_categories_overview_category as scoc
	join glue.core.search_categories_overview as sco on scoc.search_categories_overview_token=sco.search_categories_overview_token and scoc.search_category_id=sco.best_offer_category_id 
	join MinDurations md on scoc.search_categories_overview_token=md.search_categories_overview_token and scoc.duration_till_pickup=md.min_duration
	WHERE scoc.created_hour >= TIMESTAMP '2023-09-01 00:00:00.000' and scoc.created_hour < TIMESTAMP '2023-10-01 00:00:00.000'
		and sco.created_hour >= TIMESTAMP '2023-09-01 00:00:00.000' and sco.created_hour < TIMESTAMP '2023-10-01 00:00:00.000'
)

select count(*) as total_count, 
	SUM(CASE WHEN is_ok = FALSE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS best_offer_not_fastest,
    SUM(CASE WHEN is_ok = TRUE THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS best_offer_fastest
from MinCheck;
{code}



h3. CONCLUSION

it’s fairly safe to ignore corner case

I want to inform you that the updates to the ZAF Annual Vacation system are now in production.

Previously, our time-off plan followed the calendar year, running from January to December, with a carryover period of 6 months, also aligned with the calendar year. 

However, this arrangement did not comply with the carryover regulations mandated in South Africa. In South Africa, employees are required to have a carryover period determined by their anniversary date. As you may recall, previously, everyone's carryover would expire in July, irrespective of their anniversary date.

Now, your annual leave balances have been adjusted to conform with South African local laws. This transition involves changing from a "calendar year" to an "anniversary year" format. With this change, your balances were recalculated based on your anniversary period. 

In your case, your anniversary period is from August to August (because you were hired in August) and then add 6 months of carryover. Your carryover expires on February 1st. 

So at the end of your period (August 2024) you have 19 days of vacation to use.

Ksenia

I would however still suggest going with the compensation guidelines outlined in the file shared by [~accountid:5d428bce7e09400be06c040c] for UK market for the following issue types:

*Driver exceeded ETA*

While I understand the need for globalization of processes, we observe that UK consistently falls behind in CSAT results behind other markets, even as we have crucially increased our quality factor results. UK CSAT remains at 63% (and actually dropped MoM) while quality factors have improved by 5% MoM on average.

UK has notoriously demanding clients - a bit more so than in a lot of markets we have at Bolt, which is evident via the CSAT. As we continue to improve our PA scores - up to 97% in W40 - and reduce our CS Cost footprint through compensation accuracy, our CSAT has been reducing in tandem.

With the project, we are reacting to the trends we see from our clients. It appears that our current compensation guidelines are not sufficient for us to maintain satisfactory CSAT, and we need to rethink compensation guidelines - with 97% PA, we are at a point where quality factor increases won’t show a significant improvement on CSAT anymore.

With market-specific guidelines for the above issues, we will able to target user dissatisfaction more precisely, and considering volumes for these issues and current CSAT, we could reasonably expect overall market CSAT to improve by anywhere between 1% and 5%. 

As we already have market-specific refund guidelines and majority of most commonly used processes in the market are country-specific, I believe it wouldn’t be a stretch to add these minor compensation rules to the existing processes 🙂

This is a world wide accounting concept called “rounding”. It is a glitch that is not unique to Bolt. To explain it briefly, we show the balance entries with 2 decimals in admin (i.e. 31.78), however in the system it has more decimals (i.e. 31,784). And in Driver Portal, it is shown with 1 decimal only (i.e. 31.8). So when decimals get less, the system rounds it up/down to the closest number.

So, the system rounds the actual number up/down according to the decimals, which might result in cent differences. Our accounting system is smart enough to consider this number for the next payout.

User cannot reserve a vehicle/order a trip due to negative Bolt Balance
If the user has a negative Bolt Balance and travels to a country with a different currency, they won't be able to view their balance on the app anymore. Therefore, they won't be able to add funds to it or clear the debt. To resolve this issue, follow the steps outlined below:
*Step 1: Confirm charge details*
** Open User Balance > [Transaction history|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/user-balance/trxHistory] in Admin Panel
** Confirm there’s been a charge that caused a negative balance
** Look for a Booking that has: 💳 failed 🟢success
** Open the ride that caused the charge and check the date
* *Step 2: Verify the cause*
** Open the Fraud > Calculations > [User page|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/userCalculationResults]
** Look for a decision REJECT TOP UP
*** To ensure that the user cannot use the app because of debt, check for rows created on the same day or within one day.
** Is there a REJECT TOP UP decision?
*** If yes, refund the trip that caused the debt to the user’s Bolt Balance
*** If not, don’t refund the trip; advise the user they can use the app.


If you need any further information, let me know. Best Regards,

Hey, [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2]! Our external counsel came back with his input regarding issues raised by you:

# *Whether Bolt can rely on partial refund when there is a mix of benefits:* we are able to issue only a partial refund as long as we comply with the legal requirements for partial refund mentioned previously. However, we need to be able to justify the calculation of the proportion that we will refund/keep (if we cannot do this we will have to refund the full amount). The external counsel believes that as it may be difficult to calculate the correct amount of refund for the unlimited benefits and it was our decision to enter into the contract with such type of benefits, the cost of that decision is our responsibility. He, however, suggest some practical tips that we may use in combination or select just the most suitable one:
## Set a price for “unlimited” and “limited” benefits. For example, if the subscription fee is €10/month we may set costs, for example, €5/month for the limited benefits and €5/month for the unlimited benefits. We will then be able to recover a proportionate amount.
## If we only have the unlimited benefits, we can set 100 rides/deliveries for the price of the subscription fee and every other unlimited benefit (ride/delivery) is then offered for free. So, this will enable us to calculate the proportionate amount.
# *Explicit consent:* the external counsel notes that Slovak Act imposes stricter obligations than the Directive and we need to meet three obligations if the service will commence before the expiry of the withdrawal period:
## *Advise* - we need to inform the User that by giving consent to the commencement of the provision of the service prior to the expiry of the withdrawal period, the User loses the right of withdrawal upon complete provision of the service;
## *Explicit consent* - the User has to give an explicit consent to the commencement of the provision of the service prior to the expiry of the withdrawal period. 
## *Declaration* - the User has to make a declaration that they were duly advised as per (a).

* The external counsel thinks that by adding information to the T&Cs we comply only with our obligation to advise. I understand that the same applies to the fact that we add information on the app’s page shared by you.
* The explicit consent and declaration have to be separate from the advising part as decision not to give explicit consent and declaration should not prevent the User from subscribing to our service. In case the User does not give an explicit consent and declaration, they should be informed that they will not be able to use the benefits for the first 14 days despite having paid the full amount of the subscription. Therefore, we need to have a mechanism that will allow them to pay, subscribe and consent to our T&Cs, but at the same time we need to separately ask them to consent and give declarations and if these are not given, then the money is paid, but the serivice should not be provided:melting_face: 



This piece of advice creates even more questions, at least for me 😄 For example, I would ask:

# Do we need to include our benefits calculation logic to the T&Cs to be able to issue a partial refund or it is enough that we have it in the backend and stick to it when we issue a refund?
# The counsel advised that due to the fact that we offer mixed types of benefits we will not be able to use option “no refund” when the User utilises fully any limited benefit and will still be able to benefit from unlimited benefits. This “no refund” option can be used only if the only available benefits are limited and these have been fully utilised.
Therefore, why do we need to inform Users that they will lose their right to withdraw upon complete provision of the benefits if this cannot apply to them due to the nature of the service in question? Perhaps we need to add this wording anyway for some reason. However, according to the Directive and as it seems to me, if we will use only “full refund” and “partial refund” options we should inform the User only about the fact that they will need to compensate Bolt in case they choose to start using the benefits before the end of the withdrawal period for the benefits used (which are calculated in proportion). Although, I understand that for “partial refund” option we still need their explicit consent and declaration that they have been informed.

Would you like me to raise these additional questions with the counsel, [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2]? Do you have any additional questions?

Hi [~accountid:60b2030ffe01e80069c64f5f] ! Finally, after the assessment of the local laws, we have the following information for you:

*1] Opt in/opt out consent requirements:1.1. (SA)*

* *Legal position*: South Africa has an _opt-in_ for the marketing of third party products or services. Opt out model is only possible if the marketing relates to *Partner's own* similar products or services, which is not our case.
* *Risk*: Low/Medium. While the law prescribes that an opt-in would be required, we would like to note that the risk (for Bolt) of proceeding on an opt-out basis to a Partner's existing customers is low/medium due to the fact that the Regulator is currently not very active in direct marketing enforcement, and if the Regulator were to receive a complaint, it would first issue an enforcement notice before issuing any fine. Further, because the Partner is the one conducting the marketing, it would be primarily responsible for the lawfulness of the marketing.

*1.2. (KE)*

* *Legal position*: in Kenya, the law mandates an _opt-out_ model for all direct marketing communications. This applies whether promoting Partner's own products or those of another party. Additionally, a straightforward opt-out method must be available for individuals who wish to decline such marketing messages.
* *Risk*: {{Low.}}

*1.3. (GH)*

* *Legal position:* Ghana requires _opt-in_ consent, but doesn't differentiate between the marketing of Partner's products and services, and that of a 3rd party. Therefore, *Bolt should be able to rely on the previously obtained consent that the recipients gave to the Partner to market Bolt's products/services.*
* *Risk*: {{Medium. }}Due to the legal ambiguity, and the fact that the Regulator is currently not very active in direct marketing enforcement. Further, because the Partner is the one conducting the marketing, it would be primarily responsible for the lawfulness of the marketing.

*1.4. (TZ)*

* *Legal position:* Tanzania requires _opt in_ consent, but doesn't differentiate between the marketing of the Partner's products and services, and that of a 3rd party, similarly to Ghana. Therefore, *Bolt should be able to rely on the previously obtained consent that the recipients gave to the Partner to market Bolt's products/services.*
* *Risk*: {{Medium. }}Due to the legal ambiguity, and the fact that the Regulator is currently not very active in direct marketing enforcement. Further, because the Partner is the one conducting the marketing, it would be primarily responsible for the lawfulness of the marketing.

*2] Additional requirements:*

*2.1.* For (SA), (KE), (GH), the local laws will require the Partner to *disclose the details of the identity of the person* (Bolt) on whose behalf the communication has been sent, which should not be a problem in our case.

*2.2.* For (TZ), the following additional requirement will apply to the Partner:

*  disclosing the *precise purpose* of the communication (can be generally indicated that this is a promotional message);
* the communication should give out the *breakdown of the total cost* of any product or service that is the subject of the communication.

*3] General considerations:* We advise to make sure that any contractual arrangement between Bolt and the partner excludes Bolt`s liability for Partner`s compliance with the applicable data protection laws. You can reach out to us with a separate ticket when you get to this stage so we could provide our assistance.

As per test plan above some patterns I discovered:

* Polling stability drastically changes depending if device is charging or not → hints that device battery settings must play big role keeping task active on the background
** here the behaviour differs depending on a device, for example:
*** Sunmi - keeps polling (test ran for ~2.5hrs without any drop in polling) and no differences if device is charging or not.
*** OnePlus - polling is stable when charger is attached. Keeps polling for ~5 minutes when disconnecting charger. 
*** Tecno - keeps polling fine while charging. Polling becomes unstable immediately when not charging, example:
!Screenshot 2023-10-13 at 10.21.04.png|width=43.098837394385185%!
*** Samsung - keeps polling despite charger disconnected.
* There isn’t any noticeable difference between app foreground/background, problems start to appear once device is locked.

Long time ago, when there was {{PL}} project in Jira (which is now archived unfortunately), we attempted to do exactly that. However, we couldn’t figure out how to introduce this change gradually, and instead we created diagnostics to see which compilation errors still remain, if we were to compile the codebase in strict mode.

This was done via a GH Action, but since we did nothing with this information it became useless. Also, workflow itself broke and we just decided to remove it instead: [https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/pull/1331/files|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/pull/1331/files]

However, with the suggested plugin, it seems feasible to revive this initiative and to start migrating gradually. For starters, we can enable this plugin and exclude all of the subfolders which cause issues explicitly. We’ll have a very long list in the beginning, but at the very least we’ll make sure that new functionality will have to follow strict compilation. And then maybe with time we will start removing folders from the exclude list one by one, in a similar manner to what’s planned with the generator toleration report in {{bolt-server}} (as we will eventually start lowering the number of allowed errors and warnings).

Driver/Fleet is not able to see their bonuses/campaigns in the commission invoice:

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission (Ukraine migrated in Nov 1, 2022). Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890/Commission+Netting].

Dear _-NAME-_

Thank you for your request which was received by us on 5 October 2023.

As requested, please find below the information you requested under Article 15 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) concerning what personal data we process about you for the purposes of issuing a warning for reckless driving.

*What personal data do we process?*

When you use our Bolt rental electric scooters, we process your personal data collected via the sensors of the scooter to ensure you are using our services in a safe manner. The type of data we process from scooters includes geolocation data, vehicle speed, motor power (including voltage and throttle level) and driving style information (including sudden braking or skidding). This data is used to identify reckless driving events, ie. skidding, abrupt braking, tandem riding, bad parking, falls and collisions. 

*How do we process your personal data?* 

Our internal monitoring system tracks each event that occurs whilst a user is using the scooter, assigns it a certain weight, then calculates an overall score for reckless driving and issues a warning once the user reaches a certain score threshold. The total score of the user is the sum of the reckless events over the last five rides.

If we detect any potentially dangerous behaviour then we will issue the user with a warning in the app to encourage them to refrain from using the scooter in a certain way. There are three levels of warnings: 

# first warning - informs the user about the risks of misbehavior; 
# second warning - limits the speed of the scooter until the overall user score improves; and 
# third warning - temporarily suspends the user from the service. The user is able to contest the suspension by contacting our Customer Support Team for further information as to why their account was suspended.

For safety considerations, we cannot disclose the exact thresholds that trigger our warnings to prevent users from abusing the system.

*Why did you receive a warning?* 

On the day you received the warning, your ride score was high because we detected 1 skidding occurrence and 10 falls. 

We hope you found this information useful and easy to understand. If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.



Best regards

Bolt Customer Support Team

[~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] The comments for AT and HU are included in the spreadsheet respectively. Below is a short summary of the retention periods.

*Hungary:*

Under the Hungarian Civil Code, civil law claims are subject to a limitation period of *5 years*. The limitation period starts when the claim becomes due. 

Under the Labour Code, labour law claims are subject to a limitation period of *3 years*.    

However, if damage is caused by a criminal offence:

a) compensation for the damage or b) payment of damages for injury to person in connection with a personal injury, shall be subject to a limitation period of *5 years*.

*Austria:*

Generally employment-related claims (e.g. remuneration or compensation claims) are subject to the *3-year* limitation period. The common limitation period for civil law claims for damages is also *3 years* (from the time when the damage and the damaging party become known; the absolute limitation period is *30 years* from the occurrence of the damage). Shorter forfeiture periods could be agreed in the contracts.

In specific cases other limitation periods may apply and Bolt may be subject to further retention obligations. For example, documents regarding accidents at work that caused the death of the employee or an injury that lasted for more than three days must be kept for *5 years*.
